title: Heal admission reservoir tear causing multi-mode queue suffocation (customer escalations)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported bursts of 95th/99th tail latency for short requests and persistent queue saturation during mixed-length workloads. Root cause analysis shows an admission reservoir regression interacting with maintenance/cordon windows and our KV-caching eviction heuristics. Long-context requests were intermittently monopolizing inflight reservation windows; the admission reservoir failed to decay correctly when hosts entered temporary cordons, leading to sustained prefetch and KV churn that starved short flows and amplified long-context tail latency.

Why this is urgent: Several customers filed escalations with production impact (timeouts and perceived outage for low-latency endpoints). The behavior appears in all hosting modes but manifests differently: Hosted shows global latency spikes during regional maintenance, Dedicated customers saw throughput cliffs during autoscaler cycles, and Private customers observed queue build-up across upgrade windows.

Scope: Affects mixed-length workloads where a minority of long-context flows (>4096 tokens) coexists with high-velocity short flows. Reproducible with synthetic traffic that includes periodic long sequences and tenant microbursts.

Telemetry references: latency heatmaps (console: /dash/runtime/latency/2026-02-25), inflight reservation traces (trace IDs sampled at escalation times), KV eviction counters spiking in tandem with admission-window anomalies.

acceptance_criteria: Scheduler admits short requests within SLOs under mixed workloads (95th token latency <= baseline + 15%)
KV eviction burst rate reduced by >=80% during maintenance-induced cordons in synthetic repro
Canary rollout shows no regression in throughput for Dedicated reserved pools
Private upgrade package includes migration script and verification checklist
steps_taken: 2026-02-28: Oncall triaged escalation, captured traces and started a synthetic repro with mixed-length traffic
2026-03-01: Confirmed admission-reservoir counter did not decay when hosts transitioned to cordon state (repro step: cordon host + start long-context flow)
2026-03-02: Deployed temporary mitigation to Hosted: enforced per-tenant inflight cap and disabled aggressive prefetching (hotpatch) - immediate reduction in short-flow timeouts observed
2026-03-04: Implemented scheduler fix: time-decaying admission reservoir and admission-token-bucket with per-tenant fairness weight; added soft-eviction grace window to KV cache to prevent thrashing
2026-03-06: Unit + integration tests added for cordon transitions and admission decay; latency regression tests added to CI
2026-03-08: PR created and reviewed (runtime#4352). Security and infra reviewed change; no KMS changes required
2026-03-10: Started canary rollout on Hosted (10% of regions) and smoke validation; Dedicated manual canary scheduled for 2026-03-13
2026-03-12: Post-canary telemetry shows 60-75% reduction in KV eviction bursts and restored short-request velocity in canary regions
risks_and_tradeoffs: Introducing the admission-token-bucket adds a small steady-state latency increase for the largest long-context requests (estimated +5% in 99th token latency) in exchange for preserving short-flow SLOs
Soft-eviction grace increases memory pressure slightly; we may need to tune eviction thresholds per-host class in Dedicated/Private environments
Private deployments require explicit upgrade coordination; customers on pinned images might see delayed remediation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Hotfix): Hosted immediate hotpatch to enforce per-tenant inflight cap (completed)
Phase 2 (Canary): Deploy scheduler + KV-grace to 10% Hosted regions, monitor for 72h (in progress)
Phase 3 (Gradual): Expand to 50% then 100% Hosted regions if canary stable; run Dedicated manual canaries in reserved pools after Hosted 50%
Phase 4 (Private): Publish upgrade package and migration checklist for customers; offer assisted upgrade for high-impact customers
Phase 5 (Observability): Add tenant-level alarms and a dashboard to detect admission-reservoir imbalance and KV eviction spikes
postmortem_notes: Primary defect: admission reservoir lacked a decay path tied to host lifecycle events (cordon/drain), causing reservoir tokens to persist while capacity dropped
Secondary amplifier: KV eviction heuristic interacted poorly with prefetch; eviction churn removed hot prefixes, increasing long-request runtime and perpetuating prefetch
Process gap: Maintenance and autoscaler signals were not fully propagated to admission controllers in multi-mode hosting; build a lifecycle event bus for scheduler components

Action items: (1) lifecycle event bus RFC, (2) add deterministic replay canary for admission-related rollout changes, (3) schedule an ops runbook and a customer-communication template for similar escalations
